PlantDetective
ML Ratchet · GridSim phase 2 · trained on physics, graded on reality

PlantDetective

Give it a power unit's hourly output. It tells you what kind of plant it is, how much fuel it burns per MWh at full and part load, how low it can turn down, how fast it ramps, how often it starts and how flexibly it is run. Every answer comes with an error bar.

The network never saw a real plant while learning. It was trained on simulated units and graded on 400 real Texas units against their own EPA emissions-monitor records.

How it did on the exam

Error by length of history

Median error against the unit's whole-history CAMPD truth. Fractions (minimum load, start shares, capacity factor) as absolute points; the rest as relative error. Green: the Detective beats the best baseline in that row.

Heat input per unit-year

Error bars: do they cover?

Share of exam units whose truth falls inside the 68 % and 95 % intervals (year windows). Intervals were widened by one factor per output fitted on the 40 dev units only.

By technology (all years pooled, with context)

Combined-cycle units are reported separately because many report only the gas turbine's gross output, so their CAMPD heat rate looks like a gas turbine's (about 10) rather than the block's (about 7).

Ratchet · each rung kept only if it beats the incumbent

How it was built

1 · Simulated systems

GridSim generates power systems and dispatches them hour by hour with real demand, wind and solar shapes from 2018, 2020 and 2022. Individual units then commit themselves against those prices, or against real ERCOT prices of the same years.

2 · Measurement emulator

Each simulated unit is turned into a CAMPD-like record: partial start and stop hours, slow boiler warm-ups, load noise, summer derates, trips, combined cycles that report only the gas turbine, cogeneration steam fuel, and EIA-923's own accounting.

3 · Twin test on dev

Each of the 40 dev units got a simulated twin with its own parameters, run on the same 2019 and 2021 prices. Where twin and real differed (starts, warm-ups, load spread, EIA-923 ratio), the emulator was fixed.

4 · Network and exam

A small network reads 170 features of each window (load histogram, ramps, run lengths, start shapes, daily pattern, response to the market's implied heat rate, EIA facts) and outputs each quantity with an error bar.

Rungs

Twin test: simulated twin vs real dev unit

Median twin-minus-real difference per technology (log ratio for counts and durations). Smaller is better. v1: first emulator; v2: after dev calibration.

Where it fails

    Use it

    Run the release

    unzip plantdetective-v1.0.zip && cd release && python demo.py
from plantdetective import Detective
r = Detective().infer(mw_hourly, utc_seconds, price=None, gas=None, context=None)
r['tech'], r['estimates']['pmin_frac'], r['heat_rate_curve'], r['flex_class']

    numpy only. Input: at least 30 days of hourly MW. Optional: hourly price and gas price, EIA-860/923 facts. The zip has the weights, the model card, a demo on real exam units and every training script.

    Data and credits

    EPA Clean Air Markets Program Data (CAMPD) hourly unit emissions, public domain: the exam truth. EIA-860 and EIA-923 via Catalyst Cooperative's PUDL (CC-BY 4.0). ERCOT day-ahead settlement point prices (public ERCOT market data). Henry Hub daily gas price (EIA, public domain). EIA-930 hourly balancing-authority demand, wind and solar for simulation inputs (public domain). GridSim and GridData from phases 1 of this project; RTS-GMLC technology defaults (Barrows et al. 2020). Part of ML Ratchet, github.com/dogum/ML-Ratchet.
